issue: Three differential CLIs wrote their report directly to --output, so --output equal to the captured original, the IDL or the candidate replaced that input and still exited 0. A later reader of the evidence would then hash the report instead of the program.

reproduction.fixture: a temp root holding copies of scripts/, the captured original, the IDL, the imported-lab fixtures, the token dependencies and a candidate
reproduction.base: exit 0; the 10,485,715-byte ELF (head 7f454c46) is replaced by a 3,606,349-byte JSON report (head 7b227363)
reproduction.after: exit 1, ValueError: report output aliases an input, and the ELF is byte-identical
reproduction.same_result: pump_migrate_differential.py and pump_holder_distribution_differential.py behave identically for the original, the IDL and the candidate

change: Construct pump_differential_output.PumpReport after argument parsing and publish through it, exactly as scripts/fees_admin_differential.py, fees_admin_transfer_differential.py, fees_config_differential.py and the nine PumpReport families do. The publisher refuses a destination that is an input (by resolved path, directory containment, symlink or hardlink), rejects a late alias before publishing, stages the bytes and fsyncs them, and only then replaces a prior report — so a failed run cannot truncate one.

tests.before: 1 test, 9 failing subtests against the base scripts (original, IDL and candidate for each of the three); the bounded-run control is not exercised
tests.after: 2 tests OK in 0.98s: the nine alias subtests plus one bounded real-VM run per migrate and holder script that publishes a complete receipt with no staging leftovers

related_suites.tests/test_pump_output_parents.py + test: 17 tests, 2 pre-existing rustc setUpClass errors on macOS

not_claimed: No differential result changes: the guard fires before any fixture or VM work, and the bounded runs compare one real case with zero mismatches.
